ALOS lost all power on 22. April 2011, thus ending the mission.

According to Mr. Yuri Bakhvalov, First Deputy Director General of the Khrunichev Space Centre, when the automatic command to switch off the second stage engine did not take effect, the second stage continued to operate until it ran out of fuel and as a consequence the planned separation of the third (Breeze-KM) stage of the rocket which carried the CryoSat satellite did not take place, and would thus have remained attached to the second stage. Analysis of the error revealed that it was caused by faults in the programming of the rocket, which had not been detected in simulations.
